clue.text: First thought diverted

parts.note: A is first-class, top grade, so first can give the letter A
mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: A person's first idea was led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' looks like a description of the thought, but it is the definition in its entertaining sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverted can mean entertained, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Play the fool — brass in the area too?

definitions.meaning: to fool around, behave in a silly way
brass is money, and muck goes with brass in the saying where there's muck there's brass; about means in the area

explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire saying 'where there's muck there's brass' links dirt and money, so muck around, or about, is brass in the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Messing around is behaving foolishly; the second sense reads the phrase as dirt, linked to money, lying about.

clue.text: Whisky bottle?

definitions.meaning: whisky is a ..., a strong distilled drink
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like the container for the whisky, but it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled drink, and courage or mettle is also called this.

clue.text: The last straw bad hotel is broken with

indicators.note: broken tells us the letters of bad hotel are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A bad hotel breaking down is the final indignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges BAD HOTEL; 'is' is a link and W for 'with' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A final blow that finishes something off is like the last straw that breaks the camel's back.

clue.text: Marine in base is somewhat fishy

indicators.note: in tells us the marine goes inside the word for base

parts.note: base means low or contemptible, which is mean
RM stands for Royal Marine(s)

explanation.surface: A marine stationed at a base behaves suspiciously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' looks like suspicious, but it means part fish: a merman has a fish's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea creature of legend, half man and half fish, is only partly fish-like.

clue.text: American parent keeping French from computing device

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: mom is the American word for mother
de is French for from

explanation.surface: An American mother keeps a Frenchman away from his computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' is no Frenchman in the surface: it asks for the French word for 'from'; 'keeping' holds it inside the American mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A device linking a computer to a phone line converts signals, a classic piece of computer hardware.

clue.text: Determined to make newsagents finish off stocking the Sun

indicators.note: stocking means holding goods inside, so the sun goes inside
finish off tells us the end of the news agency's name is trimmed

parts.note: Reuters is a news agency, read as news agents
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Determined to make the newsagents finish selling the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newsagents' is not a shop but a news agency; 'finish off' trims its last two letters, RS, and 'stocking' holds the Latin sun inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly set on a course of action, unwavering, is a synonym for determined.

clue.text: A small part of store with competence

parts.note: a department is part of a store, and small asks for its short form dept

explanation.surface: A small branch of the shop runs competently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' asks for DEPT, the short form of department.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled or proficient means being able to act with competence.

clue.text: It's 8 down from Memphis with California first possibility

indicators.note: possibility suggests one possible way of arranging the letters, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
I is the Roman numeral one, so first can give I

explanation.surface: A city lies in a given direction from Memphis, with California the first option.
explanation.walkthrough: A very indirect anagram: 'possibility' rearranges WITH, CA and I. 8 down is WEST-BY-NORTH: the Kansas city lies roughly that way from Memphis, Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kansas city lies to the west, a little north, of Memphis in Tennessee, matching the compass bearing at 8 down.

clue.text: Texas fort located outside New York: best change direction

indicators.note: located outside means the fort surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Fort Worth is a city in Texas

indicators.note: change tells us the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fort in Texas sits outside New York, so it is best to change direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The direction is the compass point just north of west; 'change' rearranges the abbreviation and BEST into ESTBYN, which the Texas fort sits 'located outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the 32 points of the compass, a bearing just north of due west.

clue.text: Genealogy featured in 13 10 26

definitions.meaning: a family's line of ancestry, its lineage
the rhyme at 13 10 26 is about two infants hurled down a mountainside, a going down

explanation.walkthrough: 13 10 26 is the second line of a Ruthless Rhyme by Harry Graham, in which twins are thrown off a mountain: their fall is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage or ancestry is one's line of descent, and a fall down a slope is also a descent.

clue.text: See 13
18 is these four walls and unfinished correspondence comprising eggs and veg

parts.note: the answer to 18 across is the word span
taken as written
these four walls is a phrase for one's house, one's home

indicators.note: unfinished tells us the last letter of the word for correspondence is cut off

parts.note: a letter is a piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: A rambling statement about a house, letters, eggs and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is SPAN; 'unfinished' trims the last letter from LETTER, giving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish-style dish is a thick omelette of egg with potato and onion.

clue.text: See 25
(See 25) … among the damned, batsman bowled illegally at Norfolk river to get ship with female — she queried priority of arrival in ruthless rhyme

definitions.text: she queried priority of arrival in ruthless rhyme

indicators.note: among puts the chain of pieces inside the word for the damned

parts.note: the damned are those cursed
Brian Lara is the West Indian cricket batsman
in cricket, a delivery with a straightened arm is an illegal throw, not a bowl
the Thet is a river in Norfolk, flowing through Thetford
to get means to gain or secure, to be victorious
SS stands for steamship
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Among the damned, a cricketer throws illegally by a river, then boards a ship with a woman who asks who arrived first.
explanation.walkthrough: With 25, this is the opening of Harry Graham's Ruthless Rhyme, in which twins are thrown off a mountain; 'among' sets the whole chain between the first letter and the rest of the word for the damned, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's speaker wonders which twin will reach the foot of the mountain first, a question of who arrives earliest.

clue.text: Singular old movie actor still working on TV

indicators.note: singular means the plural S at the end of the actor's name is removed

parts.note: Red Buttons was an American comic film actor, Oscar winner for Sayonara

explanation.surface: An old film actor, one of a kind, still appears on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the TV standby light: a set showing it is still on, though not playing.
explanation.definitionFit: On a TV set, a glowing standby light shows the set is still powered though not playing.

clue.text: Clone animal in theatrical romance

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: in tells us the animal sits inside the word for romance

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful lies, so a romance is a lie
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A cloned animal appears in a stage love story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' is not a love story here but a verb sense, to tell fanciful tales; 'in' puts the animal inside it. 'Clone' is a verb, to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make an exact copy of it, to reproduce it.

clue.text: Watch part of the way things are going

definitions.meaning: the works of a watch, its moving mechanism
a trend or general drift of events

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The mechanism inside a watch has this name, as does a broad trend in events.

clue.text: Strange idea in town and all over the country

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of the next words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A peculiar notion is going around town and across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges IDEA IN TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread over a whole nation is countrywide, everywhere in the land.

clue.text: Nine inches between wing tips?

definitions.meaning: an old measure, the width of a spread hand from thumb tip to little finger tip, about nine inches
the distance from one wing tip to the other, as in wingspan

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second sense, the measurement across a bird's or aircraft's wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The old hand measure of nine inches and the full width across wings both use this word.

clue.text: Junkie who administers primitive punishment

definitions.meaning: slang for someone habitually high on drugs
one who pelts an offender with rocks, an ancient form of execution

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: one who throws rocks at a condemned person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a drug user, and literally one who pelts people with rocks as a punishment.

clue.text: See 25
Eat too much Cheddar?

definitions.meaning: Cheddar in Somerset, England, is famous for its limestone ravine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheddar' looks like cheese, a fair thing to eat too much of, but here it names the famous ravine in Somerset, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to overeat, and Cheddar's famous ravine is an example of a deep valley.

clue.text: Episcopal joint?

parts.note: read whimsically, the bishop's tall pointed headdress shares its name with a woodworking corner joint

explanation.walkthrough: Not a strict double definition: the headgear is episcopal and the joint is a carpenter's, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's ceremonial hat and a corner joint cut at forty-five degrees share this name.

clue.text: Crop of animal without ultimate cover

indicators.note: without ultimate tells us the last letter of the animal is dropped

parts.note: a hare is an animal
a vest is a garment that covers the body

explanation.surface: Some animal is missing its final layer of protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without ultimate' takes the last letter off HARE, giving HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the produce gathered in a season, the yield from fields.

clue.text: Horse in quality maritime measure

indicators.note: in tells us the horse sits inside the word for quality

parts.note: tone is the quality of a sound
a nag is a horse, especially an old one

explanation.surface: A horse of fine quality is judged by a seafaring standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maritime measure' is not a nautical unit like a knot or fathom but a ship's capacity in tons; 'in' puts the horse inside the word for quality.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the carrying capacity of a ship, expressed in tons.

clue.text: Alpine outlook: hereto, maybe, protected against cold, horse moved as in front … (see 13)

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of hereto may be arranged differently

parts.note: to be rugged up is to be wrapped in a blanket against the cold
a mount is a horse one rides

indicators.note: moved signals that the letters of as in are shifted around

parts.note: the brow is the front of a hill, its top edge

explanation.surface: A mountain view, perhaps, wrapped up warm, with a horse shifted to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges HERETO into OERTHE, written O'ER THE; 'moved' rearranges AS IN into AINS. It ends 'see 13' because the rhyme carries on there.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from a high point in the Alps would be the sight from a mountaintop edge.

clue.text: See 13
